title: Change-point Detection
interviewAnswer: Change-point detection looks for structural shifts in a sequence—mean, variance or distribution changes—rather than isolated anomalous points. It is useful for regime changes, deployments and sensor failures.
keyPoints: Control false alarms vs detection delay.
why: Change-point Detection is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: Change-point detection looks for structural shifts in a sequence—mean, variance or distribution changes—rather than isolated anomalous points. It is useful for regime changes, deployments and sensor failures. Control false alarms vs detection delay. Seasonality/trend should be modeled first. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Detect when a service latency baseline permanently shifts after a deployment.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Change-point Detection have?
How would you validate Change-point Detection on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
